# Additive tuning of 2026-11-03, skills round 1 best so far, scenario 3

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5

selection: sha256:d99530b2b639bb6bdd279be2a9356a64ce2a0c8cceca354d56957f198a76a20a
read_set: sha256:2a47d5b0401ca6d3239d352781fe101f4d7ba74c60c6a0dbe460e46ae9703c4d
seed: 0
```

**This line is the `best` stage of round 1 of the skills layer, in the tuning round of the additive campaign that [#1878](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1878) asked for.** It measures scenario 3, the documents, the engine and the skills as they stand, before any rewording of a skill is screened. `tools/probe/try.sh launch` ran it from the one-line spec `additive scenario-3 tuning`. It is the `scenario-3` arm of the additive tier over the 22 probes of the tuning set, at 7 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288. The owner accepted the plan of this layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1878#issuecomment-6598068852).

**One tree, one pin, one launch.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of the pinned tree, and the engine of that tree. The pin was `33f4d601` for the whole batch. The base it is read against is scenario 2 at `329f3362`, which the owner adopted from the engine layer [on the issue](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1878#issuecomment-6599224598). The canary of 8 sessions held 6 records that named one path outside the workspace each: five searched for the `headwater` binary with `find /`, and one searched for a decision file the same way. The sandbox binds none of those paths, and the proxy refused every request except those to the API. The owner read them and [passed the canary](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1878#issuecomment-6602710590). The driver then halted 7 times on a harness failure of the kind that a usage limit causes, with 152 of 154 sessions recorded. After the plan's 5-hour limit reset, it recorded the last 2 in the same try root at the same pin. It did not launch the batch again. The `tree` digest in the identity above is the digest the assembly recorded.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 154 sessions and cost 13370 cents: the intent hook live in 0, 5 stopped at the turn cap, 1 stopped at the session budget, 151 paths outside the workspace named, 0 sessions uncounted, 0 web-tool calls. 139 of the 154 sessions used the skills layer. A session the recorder could not count adds nothing to either count, so each count is a floor.

**The result.** Scenario 3 passed 120 of the 154 sessions it graded, 78%. The base, scenario 2, passed 112 of 154, 73%, over the same 22 probes in [the engine layer's transcript](additive-tuning-of-2026-11-02-engine-round-1-best-so-far-scenario-2.md). The difference is +5.2 points, with the interval [-4.4, +14.7]. The interval includes zero, so this batch does not show that the skills add to the documents and the engine. The keep rule reads only a confirmation, and a best so far is never kept. This line is the number that each screened rewording of the skills layer is compared with.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, a configuration directory that holds a copy of the credentials and nothing else, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The owner approved $1,300.00 for this layer. The driver ran this try with a cap of 15000 cents and a session budget of 300 cents.

**What the batch cost.** The driver charged 13701 cents against its cap, and the 154 recorded sessions account for 13370 cents of that sum. The difference is the sessions that recorded nothing because the harness halted them. The first best so far of a layer is charged to the base ceiling, so `try.sh spent` counts the 13701 cents against the base ceiling of 30000 cents, and the tries have spent 0 of their 100000.

**Where the raw recordings are.** The raw session logs are outside git, under `/mnt/build/hw-1878/skills-r1-best/a/sessions/L1-*/raw.jsonl` on the host that ran the batch. Nobody deletes them until the report of [#1779](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1779) is published.

**Where the other figures are.** The rate and the interval of each probe are in the generated result that reads this transcript.

```yaml
      argument: "{\"command\":\"cd /tmp && cat > orig_language.rs << 'EOF_MARKER_UNIQUE_9f3a'\\n// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0\\n//! A Document-origin check: the controlled language a kind declares.\\n//!\\n//! [Spec 12](../../../../docs/spec/12-check-layer.md#the-five-origins-of-a-check)\\n//! lists normative language among the Document-origin examples, and a language\\n//! regime is where a taxonomy says which prose rules its documents obey.\\n//!\\n//! # The declaration this rule was written for is already committed\\n//!\\n//! `.headwater/overlay.yml` declares `regimes.language.ste_house` with\\n//! `controlled: ASD-STE100, profile: house`, binds it to three kinds, and says\\n//! in a comment what was wrong with that: \\\"`tools/ste-lint.py` is the thing\\n//! that enforces it today ... the rule is in CLAUDE.md today, which is a place\\n//! no check can read\\\". This rule is the place a check can read.\\n//!\\n//! # A profile the engine does not know skips, and says which one\\n//!\\n//! `language_regime` marks `controlled` a gap in the meta-schema, for a stated\\n//! reason: spec 2 names `none`, `ste-house` and `ste-strict`, this repository\\n//! writes `ASD-STE100` with a separate `profile`, and a closed set in the\\n//! language would refuse a committed source. So the engine matches the pairs it\\n//! knows, and an instance that meets any other pair **skips with a reason that\\n//! names it**. That keeps the gap visible per document. A regime whose\\n//! `controlled` is `none` generates no instance at all, because there is\\n//! nothing to be held to.\\n//!\\n//! # What the house profile holds prose to\\n//!\\n//! Three rules, and each one is an exact match rather than a judgment. Two of\\n//! the three are the reason [`headwater_doc::sentences`] exists.\\n//!\\n//! - **Sentence length**, ASD-STE100 writing rule 6.3 for descriptive text.\\n//!   Advisory: the remediation is a rewrite, and\\n//!   [spec 4](../../../../docs/spec/04-assurance-model.md#where-promotion-cannot-finish)\\n//!   makes that permanently advisory whatever the precision turns out to be.\\n//! - **No contraction.** An error, because the expansion is mechanical and\\n//!   total, which is the bar [spec 12](../../../../docs/spec/12-check-layer.md#fixability)\\n//!   sets. A patch rides along for the endings whose expansion is one word.\\n//!   [`EXPANSIONS`] is that table, and the paragraph below says which endings\\n//!   are not in it.\\n//! - **No semicolon in running prose**, ASD-STE100 writing rule 8.1. Advisory,\\n//!   on the same bar: the remediation is to decide which clause carries the\\n//!   sentence, and no rewrite of that kind is mechanical. Running prose is a\\n//!   paragraph or a list item, and never a heading or a table cell, where a\\n//!   semicolon separates items rather than joins clauses.\\n//! - **The spelling variant the tag declares.** An error on the same terms. The\\n//!   tag is data and the word list is not, which is the same split as the voice\\n//!   patterns and is recorded in spec 13 as one gap rather than two.\\n//!\\n//! # Not every contraction has one expansion, and the split is per finding\\n//!\\n//! `doesn't` is `does not` and nothing else. `it's` is `it is` or `it has`, and\\n//! `he'd` is `he had` or `he would`. Only a reader of the sentence decides\\n//! those, so they fail the mechanical-and-total bar that the two above meet.\\n//!\\n//! [Spec 12](../../../../docs/spec/12-check-layer.md#fixability) puts the bar on\\n//! the **fix** rather than on the rule, and [`crate::Finding`] carries the patch\\n//! per finding, so the split needs no second rule and no second severity. A\\n//! contraction in [`EXPANSIONS`] carries a patch. One outside it carries the\\n//! same error with remediation prose, and a person writes it out.\\n//!\\n//! # This rule does not retire `tools/ste-lint.py`, and the PR that added it\\n//! says what still keeps the Python alive\\n//!\\n//! The memory note is that the lint hooks are interim scaffolding to be retired\\n//! into this layer rather than grown.
```
